overview: Alstom is a France-headquartered global leader in rail transport, designing, manufacturing and servicing rolling stock (trains, trams, metros), signalling systems, and turnkey integrated transport systems. The group was transformed in scale by its January 2021 acquisition of Bombardier Transportation, becoming one of the two or three largest rail equipment companies in the world alongside Siemens Mobility and CRRC. Alstom operates through four product lines (Rolling Stock, Services, Signalling, Systems) across more than 60 countries, with roughly 88,000 employees and FY2025/26 sales of EUR19.2 billion against a backlog of EUR104 billion (fiscal year ends 31 March).

business_model.summary: Alstom earns revenue from long-cycle, project-based rolling stock and systems contracts (design, manufacture and delivery of trains, trams, metros and turnkey transit systems) plus a growing base of recurring, higher-margin Services and Signalling revenue (maintenance, overhaul, spare parts, digital/CBTC signalling). Rolling Stock is the largest segment (~52-53% of sales/orders); Services (~23-24%) and Signalling (~13-14%) provide more stable, aftermarket-like income; Systems (~9%) covers large integrated turnkey projects. Backlog of EUR104bn (5.4x annual sales) gives multi-year revenue visibility, but margins depend heavily on execution quality of long-duration, fixed-price contracts.
business_model.customer_type: B2G/B2B - almost entirely public transit authorities, national railways, and infrastructure operators; very long sales cycles and multi-decade customer relationships (maintenance contracts spanning 15-45 years)
business_model.geographic_mix: Sales: Europe ~61%, Americas ~17%, Asia-Pacific ~13%, Africa/Middle East/Central Asia ~9% (FY2025/26). Backlog: Europe 59%, Americas 16%, Asia-Pacific 12%, Africa/Middle East/Central Asia 13%

competitive_position.market_position: Alstom considers itself ranked first in the global addressable passenger rail market across all continents (excluding China) following the Bombardier Transportation acquisition, which closed in January 2021 and consolidated the industry. Siemens Mobility is the main global competitor, strong in DACH region, the US and UK, with signalling/MaaS digital focus. CRRC is the largest rail manufacturer by revenue but is overwhelmingly focused on its protected domestic Chinese market, with growing but still modest international ambitions (Latin America, Middle East, SE Asia). Hitachi Rail expanded materially via the 2024 acquisition of Thales's transportation signalling business. Stadler Rail and CAF are smaller, faster-growing niche competitors increasingly diversifying into signalling and systems.

moat_factors.description: 150,000+ vehicles in commercial service worldwide and a global industrial/engineering footprint across 207 sites in 61 countries create switching costs and a large service annuity
Maintenance contracts spanning 15-45 years lock in recurring, higher-margin revenue tied to rolling stock originally supplied by Alstom or legacy Bombardier/Alstom fleets

Rail signalling and rolling stock require lengthy homologation/certification processes in each country, creating barriers for new entrants but also a source of execution risk and delay for Alstom itself
9,355 granted patents, leadership in CBTC (Urbalis), ETCS/ERTMS signalling standards, and very high-speed train platforms (Avelia Horizon)

Deep, multi-decade relationships with national rail operators (SNCF, Amtrak, Deutsche Bahn, etc.) and status as a national industrial champion in France support order flow, but can cut both ways amid political/governmental scrutiny

weaknesses: Execution quality has been inconsistent since the Bombardier integration - management itself has flagged recurring delays, cost overruns, and homologation slippage on flagship platforms
Thin margins (adjusted EBIT margin ~6%) relative to the capital and working-capital intensity of the business, leaving little buffer for project overruns
Heavy exposure to public-sector budgets and political decision-making, which can delay or cancel large contracts
Complex multi-site industrial footprint inherited from Bombardier still being rationalised (Mannheim, Hennigsdorf restructuring ongoing), creating near-term execution and cost friction
CRRC's lower cost base and Chinese state backing represent a long-term competitive threat if China's international rail ambitions scale further outside its protected home market

growth_drivers: Record FY2025/26 order intake of EUR27.6bn (+39% actual, +42% organic), led by Rolling Stock (+90%) and Systems (+288%), driving book-to-bill of 1.4x and a record EUR104bn backlog

Secular tailwinds: population growth, urbanisation, decarbonisation policy, and modal shift from cars/trucks/planes to rail support long-term public investment in rail infrastructure and fleet renewal

Growing share of rolling stock contracts attached to long-term service agreements, increasing the recurring-revenue mix and improving backlog profitability (gross margin in backlog up to 18.0% from 17.8%)

US market momentum: major commuter rail contracts won in New York (LIRR/Metro-North) and New Jersey (NJ Transit), plus Amtrak NextGen Acela entering commercial service, strengthening the Americas order book (+129% actual)
Digitalisation and signalling upgrades (ETCS/ERTMS rollout in Europe, CBTC expansion such as Urbalis Fluence) represent a long-duration structural growth segment

New CEO Martin Sion's operational turnaround plan, with a comprehensive strategy and medium-term financial targets to be presented at a Capital Markets Day in early 2027, is a near-term catalyst if credible
Hydrogen and battery-electric rolling stock (acquisition of Cummins' rail hydrogen fuel cell activities) extends Alstom's green mobility product range into non-electrified networks

business.description: Management has explicitly flagged that industrialisation of flagship rolling stock platforms is taking longer than expected, with homologation milestones deferred and insufficient alignment between development, industrialisation and manufacturing across sites - a direct driver of the FY2025/26 profit miss

business.risk: Tender management / quality of order intake risk
business.description: Large, long-duration fixed-price contracts carry margin and risk-profile uncertainty at signing that can only be corrected over many years
Heavy reliance on a complex multi-tier supply chain for components (traction systems, bogies, batteries) exposes Alstom to supplier delays, quality issues and concentration risk
Group has had to recruit nearly 9,500 permanent staff since April 2025 to support the backlog ramp-up, raising execution and training risk

financial.description: Significant non-euro revenue exposure (USD, CAD, GBP, INR, AUD, SAR); FX translation reduced FY2025/26 orders, sales and backlog by several hundred million euros to over a billion euros

financial.risk: Bonding capacity, leverage and liquidity risk
financial.description: Despite successful deleveraging (net debt ~EUR404m at March 2026, down from a peak near EUR3bn post-Bombardier), Alstom's business model requires large performance bonds/guarantees and remains rated only Baa3 (Moody's, stable outlook) - a downgrade would raise funding costs and could constrain bonding capacity

Free cash flow is highly seasonal and sensitive to contract milestones; H1 FY2026/27 is guided to consume ~EUR1.5bn of cash, and FY2025/26 FCF of EUR336m came in well below prior guidance of ~EUR1bn+ ambitions

regulatory.description: 2-3% of backlog and sales are in Middle East countries affected by regional conflict; management flags inflation, energy price volatility, and supply chain disruption risk, partially mitigated by fixed-price energy contracts and escalation clauses on ~72% of backlog
FY2026/27 guidance explicitly assumes continued ability to mitigate fluctuating tariffs, implying this is an active and monitored risk, particularly for US-exposed contracts
Risk of cyberattacks against both Alstom's own networks and its products (train control/signalling systems) is a named top-tier enterprise risk given increasing digitalisation of rail systems

macro.description: Alstom's customer base is almost entirely public transit authorities and state railways; government budget constraints, fiscal austerity or political change can delay or cancel large multi-year rail investment programmes

Higher-for-longer rates raise financing costs for customers' large capex programmes (metro, high-speed rail) and for Alstom's own working-capital funding, though direct balance-sheet interest exposure has fallen with deleveraging

execution.description: New CEO Martin Sion (ex-ArianeGroup, no prior rail industry background) took over 1 April 2026 from long-tenured Henri Poupart-Lafarge; he has publicly stated the company's FY2025/26 performance fell short and a new operational plan is required, creating both turnaround opportunity and transition-execution risk

Industrial footprint rationalisation (Mannheim, Hennigsdorf, consolidation of engineering sites) is still in progress five years after the 2021 acquisition closed, suggesting integration costs and disruption have not fully normalised

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global rail market is forecast to keep growing across all major regions through 2027-2029, with Africa-Middle East (+7.6%), Eastern Europe and Latin America cited as highest-growth regions and Western Europe remaining the largest market, led by Germany. Structural demand drivers include population growth and urbanisation (world population +2bn by 2050), decarbonisation policy (rail transport cited as lowest-carbon motorised mode per passenger-km), and post-COVID recovery of passenger traffic and operator budgets above pre-pandemic levels.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-low revenue cyclicality given multi-year public infrastructure backlogs, but margin and cash flow are cyclical/lumpy due to large project milestone timing and working capital swings; order intake can be volatile quarter-to-quarter depending on large contract award timing
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - higher rates raise the cost of debt-financed public transit capex (indirect demand risk) and Alstom's own working-capital financing costs, though direct balance-sheet exposure has fallen materially post-deleveraging

recent_developments.event: Preliminary FY2025/26 results showed record order intake of EUR27.6bn (+39%) but a profit warning: adjusted EBIT margin of ~6% missed prior ~7% guidance, and medium-term 8-10% margin ambition was pushed out; shares fell sharply on the announcement
Martin Sion (formerly CEO of ArianeGroup) announced as incoming CEO, succeeding long-tenured Henri Poupart-Lafarge who did not seek a further term; Sion officially took over on 1 April 2026

Full FY2025/26 annual results confirmed: sales EUR19.2bn (+4%/+7% organic), adjusted EBIT margin 6.1%, net income EUR324m (vs EUR149m prior year), free cash flow EUR336m (within guided EUR200-400m range), net debt reduced further to ~EUR404m
FY2026/27 outlook issued: book-to-bill above 1, sales organic growth ~5%, adjusted EBIT margin ~6.5%, positive free cash flow, with ~EUR1.5bn of seasonal cash consumption expected in H1
Alstom reaffirmed FY2026/27 guidance (book-to-bill >1, adjusted EBIT margin ~6.5%, positive FCF) in a trading update ahead of Q1 FY2026/27 results

Large US order wins: ~EUR2.0bn contract for 316 commuter rail cars for Long Island Rail Road and Metro-North, plus ~EUR1.0bn NJ Transit order for 200 Multilevel III cars and 12 dual-power locomotives; Amtrak NextGen Acela (Avelia Liberty) entered commercial service in August 2025
Acquired Cummins' rail-dedicated hydrogen fuel cell activities (including Hydrogenics GmbH, Germany), extending Alstom's green/hydrogen rolling stock product range
Industrial footprint rationalisation continues in Germany (Mannheim, Hennigsdorf); handover of the Görlitz site to KNDS completed as part of consolidating Alstom's German manufacturing footprint

guidance.as_of: FY2025/26 Annual Results / Universal Registration Document 2025/26 (filed 28 May 2026); reaffirmed in July 2026 trading update

items.notes: Reaffirmed in July 2026 trading update; FY2025/26 actual book-to-bill was 1.44x
FY2025/26 organic sales growth was 7%, so this implies some deceleration
Cut from an original ~7-8% ambition after FY2025/26 missed its own ~7% target (actual 6.1%); medium-term ambition of 8-10% margin pushed out to be addressed at a Capital Markets Day in early 2027

items.vs_prior: maintained but softer than medium-term ambition
items.notes: Guided alongside an expected H1 FY2026/27 cash consumption of approximately EUR(1.5) billion due to seasonality; FY2025/26 FCF was EUR336m
New operational KPI disclosed for FY2026/27 outlook, reflecting focus on industrial throughput after flagging production ramp-up delays in FY2025/26

Previously a nearer-term target; now explicitly a longer-term ambition contingent on converting the 18.0% gross margin in backlog, with a full operational plan and updated medium-term ambitions to be presented at a Capital Markets Day in early 2027

guidance.management_commentary: Incoming CEO Martin Sion stated the Group 'did not meet our profitability targets' in FY2025/26 due to slower-than-expected industrialisation of flagship rolling stock platforms and insufficient alignment between development, industrialisation and manufacturing across sites. He emphasized that his priority is to 'materially improve execution quality' through tighter planning discipline and improved cross-functional coordination, while noting commercial fundamentals remain strong (record order intake, robust US market, growing services attach rate). The Chairman noted the Board tasked the new management team to build a comprehensive operational plan, with rigorous Board oversight of delivery. The FY2026/27 outlook explicitly assumes no additional disruption from the Middle East geopolitical situation and continued ability to mitigate tariff fluctuations.

bull_case: Record EUR104bn backlog (5.4x annual sales) with improving backlog gross margin (18.0%, up from 17.8%) provides multi-year revenue visibility and a foundation for margin recovery if execution improves

Successful balance-sheet repair: net debt cut from a post-Bombardier peak near EUR3bn to roughly EUR400m by March 2026, removing solvency overhang and restoring financial flexibility (Baa3 stable rating)
Structural, policy-backed demand tailwinds for rail (urbanisation, decarbonisation, modal shift) support a multi-decade growth runway across all of Alstom's major regional markets
New CEO-led operational reset (Capital Markets Day early 2027) offers a credible catalyst for margin re-rating if the 8-10% medium-term EBIT margin ambition is validated with a believable roadmap

Growing recurring, higher-margin services and signalling revenue mix (more rolling stock orders now bundled with long-term maintenance contracts) should structurally improve earnings quality and reduce cyclicality over time
bear_case: Repeated profitability disappointments (FY2025/26 margin of 6.1% missed its own ~7% target; medium-term 8-10% ambition already pushed out once) raise doubts about management's ability to forecast or control execution on its complex post-merger industrial base

Execution risk remains elevated: flagship platform industrialisation delays, homologation slippage, and cross-site coordination issues were explicitly cited as root causes of the miss and are not quick to fix in a heavy-manufacturing, multi-year-cycle business
Thin absolute margins (~6%) leave very little cushion against further cost overruns, FX headwinds, or input cost inflation on fixed-price, multi-year contracts

Leadership transition risk: a new CEO without prior rail-sector experience is tasked with a turnaround of a highly technical, project-execution-driven business, with the real test (Capital Markets Day, early 2027) still months away

Heavy dependence on public-sector transit budgets and geopolitically sensitive regions (Middle East backlog exposure, US tariff risk) leaves top-line and margin assumptions vulnerable to factors outside Alstom's control
